raw_response:
The line chart displays the percentage share of employed individuals across different age groups, segmented by migration background and year of immigration. The horizontal x-axis represents age, ranging from 20 to 70 years, with tick marks at intervals of 10 years and no explicit unit label. The vertical y-axis represents the share of employed individuals in percent, ranging from 0% to 100%, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 20%. Four distinct data series are plotted: a solid black line labeled “ohne Migrationshintergrund” (without migration background), which begins at approximately 60% at age 20, rises to a plateau near 85% between ages 35 and 55, then declines sharply to below 10% by age 70; a solid gray line labeled “in Deutschland geboren” (born in Germany), which starts at about 55% at age 20, rises to approximately 80% by age 30, fluctuates between 70% and 85% until age 55, then drops to around 10% by age 70; a light blue line labeled “zugewandert bis 2009” (migrated before 2009), beginning near 35% at age 20, rising to about 75% by age 30, then oscillating between 60% and 75% until age 60 before falling to approximately 10% at age 70; and a dark blue line labeled “zugewandert seit 2010” (migrated since 2010), starting at about 38% at age 20, rising to 60% by age 30, fluctuating between 40% and 70% until age 60, then dropping sharply to 0% by age 70. All lines exhibit a general inverted U-shape with a steep decline after age 60, and all are marked with circular data point markers connected by solid lines.
